title: Taal Volcano Eruption
script: Volcano erupts, spewing ash over surrounding areas, causing widespread disruption and damage. Taal Volcano in the Philippines began to erupt on January 12, 2020, with a phreatomagmatic eruption from its main crater, as reported by the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology. The eruption produced loud rumbling sounds and ash that affected nearby regions, including Calabarzon, Metro Manila, and parts of Central Luzon and Ilocos Region, resulting in the suspension of school classes and work schedules. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology issued an Alert Level 4, indicating a hazardous explosive eruption was possible within hours to days, prompting evacuations and precautions in the surrounding areas. Volcanic activity continued into 2021 and 2022, with smaller eruptions occurring in July 2021 and March 2022, demonstrating the ongoing volatility of the volcano. The eruptions caused significant disruptions to daily life, including the suspension of school classes and flights, as well as environmental damage, such as the temporary drying up of Taal Main Crater Lake and the destruction of Vulcan Point.
